title: The Rise of Lab-Grown Meat
paragraphs: Would you eat meat grown in a laboratory? For a growing number of people, the answer is yes. Lab-grown meat, also known as cultivated meat, is real animal meat produced without killing animals. Scientists take a small sample of animal cells and grow them in a special environment.

The idea sounds like science fiction, but it is already becoming reality. In Singapore, lab-grown chicken has been approved for sale since 2020. The United States approved lab-grown chicken in 2023. More countries are expected to follow in the coming years.

Why make meat in a lab? There are several reasons. First, it is better for the environment. Traditional animal farming uses a lot of land and water. It also produces greenhouse gases that cause climate change. Lab-grown meat could reduce these environmental costs by up to 90%.

Second, it is better for animal welfare. Billions of animals are raised and killed for food every year. Many of them live in crowded and uncomfortable conditions. Lab-grown meat could end this suffering.
Third, it could improve food safety. Meat from labs is produced in clean environments. This reduces the risk of diseases that sometimes spread through traditional meat.

However, there are challenges. The biggest one is cost. Early lab-grown burgers cost over $300,000 to make. Prices have fallen dramatically, but they are still higher than traditional meat. Companies are working hard to bring costs down.
Another challenge is public acceptance. Some people find the idea of lab-grown meat strange or unappetizing. Surveys show that younger people are more open to trying it than older generations.

Despite these hurdles, investment in cultivated meat is growing. More than 150 companies worldwide are working on lab-grown meat products. The future of meat might not come from a farm, but from a laboratory.
